[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Without a governed lifecycle for creating, approving, versioning, and retiring Golden Paths, the catalog becomes an ungoverned collection of templates that diverge from enterprise standards, conflict with each other, and cannot be trusted as a constraint boundary for autonomous AI development.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Establish a formal governance model for the Golden Path Catalog that defines ownership (Platform Engineering), contribution process (proposal → review → ARB approval → publication), versioning policy (semantic versioning with breaking-change gates), and deprecation process — ensuring the catalog remains authoritative, current, and trustworthy as the constrained solution space for AI agents and developers.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Before publishing the first Golden Path to the catalog
- When onboarding a new product team to catalog contribution
- When an existing Golden Path requires a breaking change
- When retiring an outdated workload blueprint
- When evaluating whether a deviation from a path requires a new path or an exception
page_texts.7:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Enterprise Architects** defining governance frameworks and standards
- **Platform Engineers** implementing and operating governed platform capabilities
- **Solutions Architects** applying governance patterns in solution design
- **DevOps Engineers** integrating governance controls into delivery pipelines
page_texts.8:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Single source of truth**: One authorized catalog with clear ownership; no shadow catalogs or team-local templates.
- **ARB-backed trust**: Every published path has passed Architecture Review Board review, making "built from a Golden Path" a credible governance claim.
- **Controlled evolution**: Breaking changes require migration plans; no team is silently broken by an upstream catalog update.
- **AI agent reliability**: AI agents that consume the catalog are consuming a governed artifact, not ad hoc documentation.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Gainwell's [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md) establishes Golden Paths as the primary constraint mechanism for autonomous AI development. The strategy's compliance claims — that output conforming to a path inherits HIPAA, FedRAMP, and SOC 2-relevant configuration — are only valid if the catalog itself is governed. An ungoverned catalog cannot underwrite those claims.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The Golden Path Catalog does not yet exist at Gainwell. This pattern defines the governance model that must be established before the first path is authored and published. The catalog will be published via the Platform Developer Portal and consumed by both human developers (via self-service) and AI agents (via machine-readable YAML/JSON index).
page_texts.12:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Without a catalog governance model, the following failure modes are predictable:
- Multiple teams author equivalent paths independently, producing conflict and confusion.
- Paths are published without ARB review and contain non-compliant configurations.
- Breaking changes to a path silently break existing adopters with no migration support.
- Outdated paths remain in the catalog and are consumed by AI agents generating non-current code.
- There is no process for a team to challenge a path's design or propose improvements.
page_texts.13:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- The governance model must be lightweight enough to enable rapid Phase 1 delivery (5–7 paths in months 1–6) while being rigorous enough to support HIPAA/FedRAMP compliance claims.
- The same governance process applies to both human-authored and AI-assisted path authorship.
- Path versioning must be compatible with CI/CD pipeline declarations (teams pin to a path version).
page_texts.15:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

The Golden Path Catalog Governance Pattern defines the lifecycle, ownership, contribution process, and versioning model for all entries in the Gainwell Golden Path Catalog. It establishes the Platform Engineering team as the product team that owns and operates the catalog, with the Architecture Review Board (ARB) as the approval authority for publication and breaking changes.
page_texts.16:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
[Catalog Governance Lifecycle]

Contributor (team/architect)
        │
        ▼
  [1] Proposal (GitHub PR + proposal template)
        │
        ▼
  [2] Platform Engineering Review
      - Technical completeness
      - Verification Contract attached (PTN-GOV-AI-003)
      - No conflicts with existing paths
        │
        ▼
  [3] ARB Review Gate
      - Compliance scope validation
      - Standards alignment
      - Breaking change impact assessment
        │
  ┌────┴────┐
Approved  Rejected (with feedback → iterate)
  │
  ▼
  [4] Catalog Publication
      - Published to Platform Developer Portal
      - Machine-readable index updated (YAML/JSON)
      - Teams notified via changelog
        │
        ▼
  [5] Active Lifecycle
      - Quarterly review
      - Minor updates (non-breaking): Platform Engineering approval only
      - Breaking changes: return to step 2
        │
        ▼
  [6] Deprecation
      - 90-day notice to all adopters
      - Migration guide published
      - Path marked deprecated in index
      - Removed after migration window
```

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Platform Engineering Team | Catalog ownership, contribution review, publication, maintenance | ARB, Developer Portal |
| Architecture Review Board (ARB) | Approval gate for publication and breaking changes | Platform Engineering Team |
| Platform Developer Portal | Human-readable catalog publication and discovery | Golden Path templates |
| Machine-Readable Catalog Index | YAML/JSON index consumed by AI agent context systems | Developer Portal |
| Verification Contract (per path) | Mandatory accompaniment — no path published without it | PTN-GOV-AI-003 |

page_texts.18:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. A contributor (team engineer or architect) identifies a workload class not yet covered by the catalog and submits a proposal via pull request using the Golden Path Proposal Template.
2. Platform Engineering reviews the proposal for technical completeness, verifies that a Verification Contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003) accompanies it, and checks for conflicts with existing paths.
3. The ARB reviews for compliance scope, standards alignment, and breaking-change impact. They approve, reject with feedback, or conditionally approve pending specific changes.
4. Upon approval, the path and its Verification Contract are published to the Platform Developer Portal. The machine-readable catalog index is updated. Teams and AI context systems consuming the index are automatically updated at their next context refresh.
5. For subsequent changes: minor (non-breaking) updates require only Platform Engineering approval. Breaking changes (new required fields, changed defaults, removed components) require full ARB review and a migration plan for existing adopters.
6. Deprecation follows a 90-day notice period with a published migration guide before removal.
page_texts.19:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Express review**: For security-critical patches to an existing path (e.g., a CVE in a bundled dependency), a streamlined emergency review track bypasses the full ARB cycle with CISO approval in lieu of full ARB review. The path is patched and all adopters are force-notified.
- **Experimental paths**: A path can be published in `experimental` status without full ARB review for Phase 1 piloting, but cannot be used as an AI agent generation target until promoted to `active` status.
page_texts.21:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- Platform Engineering team assigned with explicit catalog ownership mandate (minimum 3 engineers)
- ARB charter updated to include Golden Path review as a standing agenda item
- Platform Developer Portal infrastructure selected or provisioned
- Golden Path Proposal Template created
- PTN-GOV-AI-003 (Verification Contract Pattern) implemented — no path can be reviewed without a Verification Contract
page_texts.23:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#phase-1-establish-governance-infrastructure-month-1]

#### Phase 1: Establish Governance Infrastructure (Month 1)

1. Update the Platform Engineering team's definition of done to require a complete Verification Contract for every Golden Path.
2. Create the Golden Path Proposal Template (GitHub PR template) covering: workload class description, compliance scope declaration, component inventory, Verification Contract attachment, and ARB review checklist.
3. Update the ARB charter to add Golden Path review as a standing agenda item with defined SLA (2-week review cycle).
4. Define path versioning policy: semantic versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`), where MAJOR = breaking change, MINOR = new optional component, PATCH = bug fix or documentation update.
5. Define path statuses: `experimental`, `active`, `deprecated`, `retired`.
page_texts.24:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#phase-2-publish-first-catalog-entries-months-16]

#### Phase 2: Publish First Catalog Entries (Months 1–6)

1. For each of the initial 5–7 Golden Paths: author path, author Verification Contract, submit via PR, complete Platform Engineering review, complete ARB review, publish.
2. Publish the machine-readable catalog index in YAML format to the Developer Portal. Include path ID, name, status, version, compliance scope, and Verification Contract reference.
3. Announce the catalog to all product teams via architecture communications. Include onboarding guide for first adopters.
page_texts.25:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#phase-3-operationalize-ongoing-governance-month-7]

#### Phase 3: Operationalize Ongoing Governance (Month 7+)

1. Establish quarterly catalog reviews: review adoption metrics, exception rates, and compliance findings per path. Identify candidates for update, expansion, or deprecation.
2. Implement deprecation process: automated notifications to all GitHub repositories declaring a deprecated path version.
3. Establish the exception management process: teams that must deviate from a path submit a formal exception request reviewed by the ARB on a defined cadence.
page_texts.26:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#governance-decision-guide]

### Governance Decision Guide

Use this guide to select the correct governance track for any catalog lifecycle event:

| Event | Review Track | Approver | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| New Golden Path (first publication) | Full ARB review | ARB | 2-week cycle |
| Security CVE patch to bundled dependency | Express review | CISO sign-off in lieu of ARB | 48 hours |
| New optional component (non-breaking) | Platform Engineering review | Platform Engineering Lead | 1 week |
| Breaking change — MAJOR version bump | Full ARB review + migration plan | ARB | 2-week cycle |
| Experimental path promotion to `active` | Full ARB review | ARB | 2-week cycle |
| Deprecation initiation | ARB notification + 90-day notice | ARB notification | 90-day window |
| Exception to a path requirement | ARB exception review | ARB | 2-week cycle |

**Choosing path status:**

| Status | Use When | AI Agent Generation Target? |
|---|---|---|
| `experimental` | Ready for piloting; ARB review pending | No — not a valid generation target |
| `active` | Full ARB approval obtained | Yes |
| `deprecated` | Superseded; migration window open | No — blocked from new generation |
| `retired` | Migration window closed; removed from index | No |

page_texts.30:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#example-3-deprecation-notice--github-issue-template-auto-generated]

#### Example 3: Deprecation Notice — GitHub Issue Template (Auto-Generated)

```markdown
## Deprecation Notice: {{ path_id }} — {{ path_name }}

> **Deprecation Date**: {{ today }}
> **Retirement Date** (90 days): {{ retirement_date }}
> **Superseded by**: [{{ new_path_id }}]({{ catalog_url }}) — [Migration Guide]({{ migration_guide_url }})

Your repository declares `{{ path_id }}` in `service.yaml`. This path will be **retired on {{ retirement_date }}**.

After retirement:
- Path removed from the machine-readable catalog index
- AI agents receive a `path-not-found` error when selecting this path as a generation target
- Conformance gates report `unknown-path` for repositories still declaring this path

**Migration steps** (~2–4 hours for a standard service):
1. Review the [migration guide]({{ migration_guide_url }})
2. Update `service.yaml` → `golden_path: {{ new_path_id }}`
3. Update `.ai/context.yaml` → new catalog URL and catalog version
4. Run: `platform-tools migrate-path --from {{ path_id }} --to {{ new_path_id }}`
5. Verify the conformance gate passes on next pipeline run
6. Close this issue when migration is complete

Support: `#platform-engineering` Slack | Office Hours: Tuesdays 2–3pm ET
```
page_texts.31:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#example-4-migration-guide-template-required-for-major-version-bumps]

#### Example 4: Migration Guide Template (Required for MAJOR Version Bumps)

Every MAJOR version bump and every deprecation must include a migration guide conforming to this structure. The guide is published at `catalog/changelogs/{path-id}/migration-{old-version}-to-{new-version}.md` and linked from the machine-readable catalog index and the deprecation notice.

```markdown
# Migration Guide: {{ path_id }} v{{ old_version }} → v{{ new_version }}

**Published:** {{ date }}
**Estimated effort:** {{ effort_estimate }} (e.g., 2–4 hours for a standard service)
**Breaking changes:** {{ breaking_change_summary }}

## What Changed

<!-- List every breaking change. Be explicit: old value → new value. -->

| Component | Change Type | Old Value / Behavior | New Value / Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scaffold.yaml` | Field renamed | `namespace_name` | `workload_namespace` |
| Verification Contract | Check added | — | `CC-009` (new Layer 1 check) |
| Infrastructure Module output | Renamed | `workload_identity_ref` | `identity_principal_ref` |

## Services Affected

This migration is required for any service repository that declares `{{ path_id }}: v{{ old_version }}` in `service.yaml`. Run:

```bash
platform-tools list-adopters --path-id {{ path_id }} --version {{ old_version }}
```

to see all affected repositories.

## Support

`#platform-engineering` Slack | Office Hours: Tuesdays 2–3pm ET | ARB exception process: GUID-GOV-PROC-002
```

- Treat the catalog as a product with a roadmap, not as a documentation repository. Prioritize paths by adoption potential.
- Never publish a path without a Verification Contract. A path without verification is a recommendation, not an enforceable standard.
- Use the machine-readable index as the integration contract with AI systems — keep it stable and versioned separately from the human-readable portal content.
- Set adoption targets per path (e.g., "80% of new HIPAA microservices use GP-001 within 6 months of publication") and track them as product metrics.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Governance overhead blocking Phase 1 velocity**: Avoid requiring the full ARB review cycle before the first path is published. Use `experimental` status to allow piloting, with promotion to `active` requiring full review.
- **Catalog drift from actual practice**: If teams consistently deviate from a path, that is a signal the path needs updating — not that teams should be penalized. Review exception patterns quarterly.
- **Breaking changes without migration plans**: Any MAJOR version bump without a migration guide will break adopters silently. The policy must require a migration guide as a hard gate on MAJOR releases.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#standards-alignment]

### Standards Alignment

- [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md) — this pattern operationalizes the catalog governance component of that strategy
- [Enterprise Architecture Verification Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-architecture-verification-strategy.md) — defines the Verification Contract requirement that gates catalog publication
page_texts.43:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

HIPAA and FedRAMP compliance claims made on behalf of Golden Paths are only defensible if the path was reviewed and approved through this governance process. The ARB review step must include explicit compliance scope validation by a qualified reviewer (Security Architecture or Compliance).

All path reviews and approvals must be traceable. GitHub PR history serves as the primary audit trail for path authorship and approval decisions.
page_texts.44:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

- New path publication: Platform Engineering review → ARB approval → publication
- Minor update (non-breaking): Platform Engineering review → publication
- Breaking change (MAJOR version): Platform Engineering review → ARB approval → migration plan published → publication
- Deprecation: ARB notification → 90-day notice → retirement

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|---|---|---|
| Catalog coverage (% of new workloads using an approved path) | ≥80% within 12 months of publication | CI/CD conformance gate telemetry |
| Exception rate (% of deployments requiring deviation approval) | <10% | Exception tracking registry |

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** Platform Engineering is authoring the first Golden Path: HIPAA REST Microservice on AKS (GP-001).
**Implementation:** The team authors the Terraform module, application scaffold, CI/CD template, security configuration, and compliance metadata. They simultaneously author the Verification Contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003). The complete package is submitted as a PR with the Golden Path Proposal Template completed. ARB reviews and approves. The path is published to the Developer Portal and the machine-readable index.
**Outcome:** The first catalog entry is published with full ARB backing. The machine-readable index is immediately available for AI agent context integration.
page_texts.48:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** A bundled library in GP-001 has a critical CVE discovered 4 months after publication.
**Implementation:** Platform Engineering triggers the express review track. The CVE patch is reviewed with CISO approval in lieu of full ARB cycle (SLA: 48 hours). The path is patched (PATCH version bump), published, and all repositories declaring GP-001 are notified via automated GitHub issue.
**Outcome:** Security response time is measured in hours, not the 2-week ARB cycle.
page_texts.49:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#real-world-example-3]

### Real-World Example 3

**Context:** GP-003 (Scheduled Batch Job) is superseded by GP-007 (Scheduled Batch Job v2 with native autoscaling and updated CronJob API). Platform Engineering initiates a formal deprecation after confirming GP-007 covers all GP-003 use cases.

**Implementation:** The machine-readable catalog index marks GP-003 as `deprecated: true` with a retirement date 90 days out. Automated GitHub issues are opened in all 9 repositories still declaring GP-003, each including the migration guide and a 2-hour estimated effort. Three teams migrate in the first 30 days. Three more complete migration at day 60 following an ARB-directed prompt. The final three complete by day 85. At day 90, the catalog index removes GP-003 from the active paths list. The AI context update pipeline automatically flags GP-003 as an invalid generation target.

**Outcome:** All 9 adopters migrate within the window with zero production disruption. Platform Engineering coordination effort is reduced by ~80% compared to the prior manual outreach model. The migration guide is reused as a template for the next two deprecation cycles.
page_texts.51:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#scenario-1-new-workload-class-identified-by-product-team]

#### Scenario 1: New Workload Class Identified by Product Team

A product team building a new Medicaid eligibility service finds no existing path covers their specific compliance requirements (dual HIPAA + FedRAMP scope). They submit a proposal for GP-NEW. Platform Engineering reviews, identifies partial overlap with GP-001, and works with the team to create a GP-001 variant with FedRAMP additions rather than a net-new path. The variant is reviewed and published.

#### Scenario 2: AI Agent Requests a Path Not in Catalog

An autonomous AI agent receives a requirement that does not map to any catalog entry. The agent halts and escalates to human architectural review (per PTN-GOV-AI-002). The architect evaluates whether a new path should be created or whether the closest existing path covers the requirement with an approved deviation.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#scenario-3-exception-management-and-catalog-improvement-feedback-loop]

#### Scenario 3: Exception Management and Catalog Improvement Feedback Loop

A product team building an integration with a third-party claims platform cannot conform to GP-001's egress network policy — the vendor requires a non-standard outbound port that the policy does not allow. The team submits a formal exception request. The ARB approves a 12-month renewable exception scoped to the specific service, records it in the compliance evidence store, and assigns a catalog follow-up item to Platform Engineering. Six months later, two more teams hit the same constraint. Platform Engineering treats the recurrence as a signal and publishes a new catalog variant (GP-001-EXT-VENDOR-INTEGRATION) covering the vendor integration pattern. The original exception is marked resolved at its next renewal cycle.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

- **Template consistency**: Five teams building HIPAA microservices independently produce five divergent configurations — encryption settings, network policies, and secret management approaches vary by team with no authoritative source of truth
- **AI generation anchor**: An AI coding agent generates a sixth implementation from training-data defaults, producing a non-enterprise variation shaped by model training rather than Gainwell standards
- **Audit surface**: A HIPAA auditor must review every individual service configuration independently; there is no catalog-level governance shortcut
- **Compliance defensibility**: "This service is HIPAA-compliant" is an assertion with no systematic evidence or formal approval history behind it
- **Update propagation**: When a security baseline changes, teams must be individually discovered, notified, and remediated with no coordinated mechanism
page_texts.56:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

- **Template consistency**: All HIPAA microservices use GP-001. Security configuration, network policy, and secret management are identical in compliance posture across every adopter
- **AI generation anchor**: An AI agent generates configurationally equivalent output by selecting GP-001 — the enterprise standard, not a training-data approximation
- **Audit surface**: A HIPAA auditor reviews one catalog entry and its ARB approval record; all GP-001 adopters are covered in a single governance review
- **Compliance defensibility**: "This service was built from GP-001 v1.2.0" is a provable claim backed by a passing Verification Contract and timestamped conformance evidence
- **Update propagation**: A GP-001 security patch is published once; all 12 adopters receive automated notifications and migrate on a coordinated schedule

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Without a governed lifecycle, the Golden Path Catalog becomes ungoverned documentation that cannot underwrite compliance claims or serve as a reliable AI agent constraint boundary.

**Solution:** Formal governance model with Platform Engineering ownership, ARB approval gates for publication and breaking changes, semantic versioning, and a mandatory Verification Contract requirement.

**When to Use:**
- Before the first Golden Path is published
- For any change to a published path (minor or breaking)
- When retiring an outdated path

**Key Benefits:**
- Every published path is ARB-approved and compliance-validated
- Breaking changes never silently break adopters
- AI agents consuming the catalog consume a governed, authoritative artifact

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** Platform Engineering team assigned, ARB charter updated, PTN-GOV-AI-003 (Verification Contract Pattern) implemented.

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-AI-002, PTN-GOV-AI-003, PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-APP-GOV-001
